sense: facts that show something is true

terms.gloss: evidence, proof; a sign from which something is inferred
evidence: Cic. Att. 10.12a.3: mihi argūmentō est rēctē esse in Hispāniīs
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: proof that rests on facts, where ratiō rests on reasoning. Argūmentō esse, to be evidence (that), with an accusative and infinitive. A sign or clue that points to something is indicium (see sign); evidence given in court is testimōnium (see evidence, in court).

terms.gloss: a proof, a lesson, an example: documentō esse, to show
evidence: Sall. Cat. 9.4 (Lewis & Short): quārum rērum maxuma documenta haec habeō
terms.comment: Classically not a document but something that teaches: a lesson, an example, a proof (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: proof, evidence (above all of guilt), information laid
evidence: Sall. C. 52.36: convictus indiciō alicujus (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Massiliēnsium factum cum ipsum per sē lūculentum est tum mihi argūmentō est rēctē esse in Hispāniīs.
phrases.english: What the people of Massilia have done is splendid in itself, and it is also evidence to me that things are going well in Spain.

phrases.latin: quod autem idem maestitiam meam reprehendit, idem jocum, magnō argūmentō est mē in utrōque fuisse moderātum
phrases.english: and the fact that the same man finds fault both with my gloom and with my joking is strong evidence that I kept the mean in both

sources: Lewis & Short: argumentum · Lewis & Short: documentum · Lewis & Short: indicium
